meta.title: Physical Features of India
meta.intro: Major physiographic divisions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.

objectives: Major physiographic divisions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.
Explain the major geographical features and processes described in the chapter.
Use maps and examples to connect physical geography with people and places.

blocks.text: The Himalayan mountains are young fold mountains and form a high natural boundary in the north.
The Northern Plains were formed by alluvial deposits brought by the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra river systems.
The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient tableland made of crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks; it includes the Central Highlands and Deccan Plateau.
The Indian Desert lies west of the Aravalli Hills. The western and eastern coastal plains flank the peninsula; the Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep groups form India’s islands.
Major physiographic divisions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.
